answer_core:
I would not choose the Silva direction yet, and I would not default to the safer lab path. Treat this as two gates that must both stay real: Silva executability and fallback survivability.

For Silva, do not count it viable until you have concrete evidence about data access, sharing terms, collaborator role, timeline, and advisor support. A hot field is not enough if those constraints cannot carry a dissertation.

For the fallback, protect the reversal target before relying on it. It is only useful if it remains advisor-backed, funded, technically ready, identity-coherent, and still available when the stop date arrives. A delayed pivot is unsafe if the fallback quietly disappears.

Sequence: advisor first, short Silva evidence probe second, committee after the data path is real. Use broad success rates only as humility checks, not probabilities for this case. Do not build a finished proposal around Silva, do not run all options in parallel, and do not let fallback comfort hide the need to test Silva's binding constraints.
